Download TEA's FIRST financial integrity ratings

txs_get_first.Rd

Returns the Financial Integrity Rating System of Texas (FIRST) ratings TEA assigns every school district (School FIRST) and open-enrollment charter (Charter FIRST): one row per district or charter per rating year, with its pass/fail status, rating, letter grade, and score. TEA publishes these only through two public search apps, not as files; each statewide workbook is fetched from those apps on demand and cached like any other download.

Usage

txs_get_first(
  years,
  type = c("district", "charter"),
  cache = TRUE,
  refresh = FALSE,
  output = c("tidy", "raw"),
  timeout = 60,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

years

Integer vector of ending rating years (2026 means the 2025-26 ratings). Required.

type

"district" (School FIRST), "charter" (Charter FIRST, including university charters), or both (the default).

cache

If TRUE, reuse a cached copy when one exists.

refresh

If TRUE, re-download even if cached.

output

"tidy" (one typed row per district or charter and rating year) or "raw" (TEA's columns as published, all character, after year, list, and tea_title columns).

timeout

Seconds per request; default 60.

verbose

Print progress messages.

Value

A tibble with columns year, school_year, fiscal_year, type ("district" or "charter"), university_charter, district (6-digit district number, zero-padded string), district_name, region (2-digit ESC region), status, rating, grade, score, release ("preliminary" or "final"), and last_updated (Date), plus a txschools attribute recording each workbook's provenance.

Years

years are ending rating years, matching TEA's labels: 2026 means the 2025-26 FIRST ratings, which TEA computes from fiscal-year 2025 (2024-25 school year) financial data. The fiscal_year column (year - 1) joins the rated data to PEIMS actuals, e.g. txs_get_peims_finance(2025, "actual").

Coverage

School FIRST covers 2002-03 onward and Charter FIRST 2011-12 onward. Since 2017-18 TEA rates university charters pass/fail in a separate list; those rows have type = "charter", university_charter = TRUE, and no score. TEA's public site has no separate university list before 2017-18.

The rating system changed over time, so compare rating and score within an era:

  • 2002-03 to 2013-14: "Superior Achievement", "Above Standard Achievement", "Standard Achievement", "Substandard Achievement" (plus "Suspended: ..." and, for charters, "Undetermined"); scores out of 65 to 85 points depending on the year.

  • 2014-15: pass/fail only ("Pass" or "Substandard Achievement"), scored out of 30.

  • 2015-16 onward: letter grades out of 100 points, "A = Superior" through "F = Substandard Achievement" (worded "A = Superior Achievement" from 2020-21; Charter FIRST writes "A - ..."). The grade column holds the letter for these years and is NA before.

Preliminary and final ratings

TEA posts preliminary ratings in August and final ratings, after appeals, by mid-November. Charter FIRST labels its workbooks accordingly, but School FIRST labels every workbook "Final". The release column therefore follows TEA's label for charters and marks a district workbook "preliminary" when it was downloaded before December 1 of the rating year. Cached copies are never replaced silently: once finals post, re-run with refresh = TRUE (the function reminds you when a cached copy predates them).

How it is fetched

Each (rating year, list) workbook takes one short session against TEA's search app, at one request per second: three requests for the district or charter list, four for the university-charter list. The full history, txs_get_first(2003:2026), is about 150 requests on first use and free afterwards.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
first <- txs_get_first(2026)
txs_get_first(2020:2026, type = "district") |>
  dplyr::filter(district == "161920")
} # }
